name: win32-toolkit
description: win32-toolkit delivers end-to-end Intune Win32 packaging: point at a winget package or any installer, scaffold a PSAppDeployToolkit v4 project, and capture real installs in a disposable Windows Sandbox or Hyper-V VM. It derives detection and uninstall logic, validates install/update paths, packages a .intunewin, and publishes to Intune with dependencies, branding, and requirements.
author: Maxime Guillemin

securityCheck.aiSummary: The codebase has legitimate admin tooling patterns but includes a potentially risky dynamic hook injection mechanism and execution policy bypass. No evidence of credential theft, data exfiltration, hardcoded secrets, or remote code execution from URLs. Recommend hardening: avoid ExecutionPolicy bypass in production launchers, restrict and sign hook/asset contents, validate and integrity-check all org hooks before ingestion, and consider minimizing on-device shell code execution by requiring signed scripts and hardened path controls.
